declaration.preface: Shilpa Medicare understands that pharmaceutical manufacturing carries a range of environmental responsibilities including management of process chemicals, solvent usage, effluent treatment, air emissions, energy consumption, water use, biodiversity impacts, and product end-of-life considerations. We are committed to conducting our operations in an environmentally responsible and sustainable manner, ensuring full compliance with all applicable environmental laws and regulations across India and internationally. Our commitment extends to our entire value chain from raw material sourcing and R&D through manufacturing, packaging, and distribution and covers employees, contractors, suppliers, and business partners. Through continuous improvement, adoption of innovative clean technologies, resource efficiency, responsible waste management, and reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, we strive to minimize our environmental footprint while delivering affordable, high-quality pharmaceutical products to patients worldwide.
declaration.declaration:
The objectives of this Environmental Responsibility Policy of Shilpa Medicare Limited are to:

Ensure full compliance with all applicable environmental laws, regulations, permits, and statutory requirements in India and all international jurisdictions where the Company operates, including the Environment Protection Act, Water Act, Air Act, Hazardous Waste Management Rules, and other applicable legislation.

Minimize the environmental impacts arising from pharmaceutical manufacturing, R&D, formulation, CDMO activities, biologics production, and associated logistics operations.

Promote efficient and responsible use of natural resources including energy, water, solvents, and raw materials through conservation measures, process optimization, and adoption of clean technologies.

Reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions through energy efficiency, renewable energy adoption, and responsible management of Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 emissions.
declaration.scope:
This Policy applies to all operations of Shilpa Medicare Limited and its group entities, Subsidiaries, Joint Ventures including API manufacturing facilities, formulation plants, R&D centers, CDMO operations, biologics units, corporate and administrative offices, and all associated with Shilpa Medicare Operational Locations. The Policy also extends to all global sales offices located in Malaysia, Austria, Dubai (UAE), the United Kingdom, Spain, and the United States of America.

It is applicable to all employees (permanent and contract), management, directors, business associates, vendors, contractors, and all internal and external stake holders working on behalf of the Company.

Energy Consumption & GHG Management: We will continue to use renewable energy such as wind power for our electrical energy requirements and biomass fuels for our thermal energy requirements. The biomass-fired boiler is registered under the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) of the Kyoto Protocol with the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change.

We strive to reduce energy consumption across all manufacturing blocks, utilities, R&D facilities, and offices by installing energy-efficient motors, variable frequency drives (VFDs), LED lighting, energy-efficient HVAC and chilling systems, waste heat recovery systems, and star-rated equipment, as well as optimizing reactor heating/cooling cycles and utilities to lower electricity and fuel usage.

We commit to work towards lowering Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions through improved fuel management in boilers and captive systems, energy conservation initiatives, and a gradual transition to cleaner energy sources across our facilities.

We will explore and increase the adoption of renewable energy including solar power and expansion of our existing wind power operations wherever technically and commercially feasible, to minimize dependence on fossil fuels and support national and global climate action goals.

We strive to minimize direct GHG emissions (Scope 1) associated with manufacturing processes, boilers, captive power generation, owned vehicles, and fuel usage through improved process efficiency, planning, and equipment maintenance.
We seek to build employee awareness on energy efficiency, GHG management, and climate responsibility through periodic training, departmental energy champions, and internal communication initiatives.

We will identify and evaluate key Scope 3 emission categories including purchased raw materials and chemicals, upstream and downstream transportation, employee commuting, business travel, capital goods, and waste generated in operations to understand and progressively reduce the Company's broader carbon footprint.

We will encourage raw material suppliers, contract manufacturers, and logistics partners to adopt sustainable practices, energy efficiency measures, and low-carbon alternatives through responsible sourcing and supplier engagement programs aligned with PSCI principles.
We are continuously implementing energy conservation programs & striving to achieving energy economies & investing in latest best available technologies.
Biodiversity Conservation & Land Use: We are committed to protecting and enhancing biodiversity in and around our manufacturing locations particularly Raichur, Karnataka by preventing soil and groundwater contamination, managing chemical and effluent releases responsibly, and maintaining a clean and green plant environment.

We will actively participate in and support the Green Raichur initiative, tree plantation drives, and other regional biodiversity and green cover programs, contributing to ecosystem restoration and local environmental well-being.

We will conduct employee awareness and training programs on biodiversity conservation to encourage responsible environmental practices and active participation in protecting and enhancing biodiversity in and around our manufacturing locations.
We will ensure responsible storage and secondary containment of hazardous chemicals and solvents to prevent accidental soil or groundwater contamination that could harm local biodiversity.
We will promote native tree plantation, green belts, and landscaping within our facility premises to enhance local biodiversity and create a healthier working environment.
We seek to integrate biodiversity risk assessment into our Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) process for any new manufacturing facility, capacity expansion, or significant infrastructure project.
Water Management & Effluent Treatment: We will conduct periodic inspection and preventive maintenance of cooling towers, condensers, reactors, plumbing systems, and water storage infrastructure to detect and rectify leakages, thereby reducing unnecessary water wastage.

We will implement and maintain robust Effluent Treatment Plants (ETPs), Multiple Effect Evaporators (MEEs), and Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) systems across applicable manufacturing facilities to prevent water pollution and ensure compliance with KSPCB, TSPCB, and CPCB norms.

We strive to optimize water consumption in manufacturing processes, utilities, laboratories, and administrative facilities through regular monitoring, water audits, conservation measures, and installation of water-efficient fixtures.
We will explore opportunities for water recycling including treated water reuse in cooling towers, scrubbers, and utilities to minimize freshwater withdrawal from bore wells and municipal sources.
We aim to maintain compliance with effluent quality standards and prevent discharge of untreated or partially treated effluents to any water body, drain, or land.

We will conduct employee awareness and training programs on water conservation, efficient water use, and responsible effluent management to promote a culture of water stewardship across our manufacturing and administrative facilities.
Materials, Chemicals & Waste Management: We have invested in developing green chemistry to reduce waste generation & develop clean & efficient processes where ever possible.

We aim to minimize hazardous and non-hazardous waste generation through process optimization, solvent recovery and recycling, source reduction, green chemistry principles, lean manufacturing, and good housekeeping practices across all API and formulation manufacturing blocks.
We strive to maximize solvent recovery through distillation, condensation, and closed-loop recycling systems, reducing both waste generation and raw material consumption.
We strive to follow the principles of Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle (3R) across all waste streams including spent solvents, process residues, packaging materials, and laboratory waste.

We seek to ensure safe handling, storage, labeling, secondary containment, and use of hazardous process chemicals, intermediates, and APIs in strict compliance with applicable Safety Data Sheets (SDS), GMP standards, and environmental regulations.

We aim to comply with all applicable waste management regulations including the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, E-Waste Management Rules, and Plastic Waste Management Rules.
We promote training of all relevant employees on waste segregation, hazardous chemical handling, spill prevention, containment, and emergency response to minimize environmental and safety risks.

We ensure that all hazardous waste is disposed of only through authorized Treatment, Storage, and Disposal Facilities (TSDFs) and that all manifests and records are maintained as per regulatory requirements.
Product End-of-Life & Environmental Prod: We are committed to responsible product end-of-life management, including providing clear, accurate, and regulation-compliant guidance to customers, distributors, and healthcare providers on the safe handling, storage, use, and environmentally sound disposal of all APIs, formulations, biologics, and CDMO products.

We will develop and promote product-specific disposal guidance including guidance on pharmaceutical waste disposal in compliance with Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules to ensure that expired, unused, or damaged pharmaceutical products are not disposed of in ways that harm the environment or public health.

We will integrate eco-design principles into packaging development including the use of recyclable, biodegradable, or reduced-material packaging to minimize the environmental impact of our product packaging at end-of-life.

We will work with authorized waste recyclers, pharmaceutical waste disposal agencies, and take-back scheme operators to support compliant and environmentally responsible end-of-life management of our products in India and key regulated markets.

We will assess and progressively improve the environmental profile of our product portfolio including API synthesis routes, excipient choices, and dosage form design to minimize lifecycle environmental impacts from manufacturing through to patient use and product disposal.
Air Pollution Prevention & Control: We are committed to preventing and controlling air emissions including VOCs from solvent usage, particulate matter from manufacturing processes, boiler stack emissions, and process vent gases through engineering controls, condensers, scrubbers, bag filters, and Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (CEMS).

We will ensure compliance with ambient air quality standards and stack emission norms as prescribed by KSPCB, TSPCB, and CPCB, and maintain all pollution control equipment in optimal operating condition at all times.

We will explore and adopt containment technologies, closed-loop solvent systems, and green chemistry approaches to minimize fugitive emissions and VOC losses during API synthesis and formulation manufacturing.

We will leverage innovative clean manufacturing technologies such as the Bipolar System adopted by our facilities from Japan to ensure pharmaceutical manufacturing processes are sustainable with minimal air pollution impacts.

We will conduct periodic air quality monitoring both at stack emission points and ambient air within and around facility boundaries and share monitoring results transparently with regulatory authorities and relevant stakeholders.
We will train all relevant manufacturing and EHS personnel on air pollution control equipment operation, maintenance, regulatory compliance, and emergency response for accidental air releases.
Climate Risk & Analysis: We conduct comprehensive climate risk and vulnerability assessments for all owned and leased manufacturing facilities, R&D centers, warehouses, and administrative offices to identify site-specific physical climate risks including extreme heat, flooding, drought, cyclones, and water stress, as well as transition risks arising from evolving regulations, carbon pricing, and changes in market and stakeholder expectations.

We regularly update climate risk assessments to reflect the latest climate science, evolving regulatory landscapes, national and state climate action policies, and changes in our operational footprint, ensuring our adaptation strategies remain relevant and effective.

We will integrate climate risk identification and assessment outcomes into our overall Risk Management framework, ensuring climate risks and opportunities are systematically reported to the Board of Directors and Senior Management for informed decision-making.
Customer Health & Safety: We ensure that all APIs, formulations, biologics, and CDMO products manufactured and supplied by Shilpa Medicare comply with applicable CDSCO, USFDA, EMA, PMDA, TGA, and other relevant regulatory requirements, maintaining the highest standards of product quality, purity, potency, safety, and environmental compliance.

We implement rigorous batch-level verification, analytical testing, stability studies, and QA/QC controls to ensure that no non-compliant, substandard, adulterated, or environmentally compromised products reach patients, customers, or distribution networks.

We seek to minimize environmental and safety risks associated with the manufacturing, storage, transportation, and use of oncology and other highly potent pharmaceutical products through the use of state-of-the-art isolators, containment systems (up to OEL Level 4), HEPA filtration, and closed transfer technologies.

We will source raw materials and chemicals only from authorized, qualified, and environmentally responsible suppliers, conducting supplier qualification audits and due diligence to prevent use of materials with unacceptable environmental or safety profiles.

We aim to provide customers, distributors, healthcare providers, and relevant stakeholders with comprehensive, accurate, and up-to-date product safety information including SDS, Certificate of Analysis, stability data, and storage and handling instructions through electronic and digital channels.

We will utilize digital platforms, QR codes, electronic batch traceability systems, and online regulatory submissions to provide real-time access to product specifications, safety certifications, and recall or quality alert information, ensuring informed and safe product usage by customers.

We maintain a robust product recall and field alert system, ensuring that any product safety or quality issue affecting customer health or environmental safety is escalated, investigated, and resolved within defined timelines, with full transparency to regulators and customers.

policy.monitoring:
Shilpa Medicare Limited is committed to the continuous improvement of its environmental performance across all manufacturing facilities, R&D centers, offices, and warehouses. Environmental considerations are embedded into day-to-day operations with the aim of systematically reducing resource consumption, minimizing waste and air emissions, improving solvent recovery, and preventing pollution at source. Key environmental parameters including energy consumption, water usage, specific waste generation, air quality and stack emissions, GHG emissions (Scope 1, 2, and identified Scope 3 categories), biodiversity indicators, and regulatory compliance status are monitored at facility level on a regular basis and tracked against the quantitative targets set out in this Policy.

Key Components of Continuous Improvement & Monitoring

Parameter Monitoring

Energy, water, waste, solvent recovery, air quality, effluent quality, GHG emissions, biodiversity, and regulatory compliance are tracked at each facility on a regular basis.

Internal & External Audits

Periodic internal EHS audits and third-party environmental audits assess compliance status, identify improvement opportunities, and verify progress against targets.

Incident Reporting & CAPA

All environmental incidents, near-misses, spills, and regulatory non-compliances are reported, investigated for root cause, and closed through the CAPA system.

Management Review

Environmental performance data is reviewed by Senior Management at least annually to assess target achievement, resource adequacy, and policy effectiveness.

BRSR & ESG Disclosure

Performance data is compiled and disclosed in the Company's Annual Report and Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) under SEBI LODR Regulations.
policy.reviewMechanism: This Environmental Responsibility Policy is reviewed at least once every year, or whenever triggered by significant changes in business operations, new or amended applicable environmental legislation, changes in regulatory requirements, material changes in manufacturing scale or technology, stakeholder expectations, or the occurrence of a significant environmental incident. The review is conducted by the EHS & Sustainability Head in consultation with Senior Management and relevant facility heads.
